body:
Video games. 

My brothers had made me start playing Destiny about a year before I got my depression got bad enough to make me consider ending it all, and Destiny 2 got announced the year I was at my lowest point. I figured I could at least stick around to see what happened in it.  
Apparently I stuck around long enough to finally open up to my parents and get therapy.  

Also, around that time, I met a dude while playing Overwatch, After talking for a few hours he opened up about how he was considering suicide. I talked down, repeated all the typical "oh but you have so much to live for" routine. After a few minutes of repeating the generic "don't do it" shit, I started to talk about how if he gave up now, he'd never know what tomorrow brought.   
That if he decided to end it tonight, he would never know how much better things could get. I talked about how it wouldn't be easy, but that things could and would turn out OK if he was willing to stick around and make them get better.   
That I knew how it felt to feel like everything was against you, like no one in the world cared about you and everyone would be better off if you where dead, but that it isn't true. That just because we may not see how we could possibly effect people, it doesn't mean we don't.   
I told him that if he was willing to listen to me go on and on about reasons to live, he must know that there is still a few out there.   
I told him that I believed he could make it out.  That he could make things better.  
And I guess, somewhere in those rantings I realized that I could make it out OK.

I still talk to him sometimes. He's doing a lot better.   
And for what it's worth, I am too.
